focus.jnote: The surface is strong but the floor is not. The S&P 500 closed at a fresh record Tuesday (~7,819, up ~0.58%) and the Nasdaq hit new highs on a chip-led rally, but futures are flat-to-lower this morning as oil rebounds and yields climb again. Three live wires remain: the US–Israel war on Iran drags on with the Strait of Hormuz still blocked and tankers struck; the 10Y sits near ~5.31%, back up after Monday's fresh 24-year high; and crude has recovered toward ~$90 (Brent ~$101) on renewed Houthi attacks and Gulf-supply risk. Gold slipped toward ~$4,120 as the dollar firmed. FOMC minutes land at 2:00 ET. This is a headline-and-rate tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into — and the scanner nearly confirmed it: only one name (PENG) cleared the criteria today.
focus.notdown: Megacap tech & AI/semis (NVDA, chipmakers) led the market to fresh records — but that's stretched momentum leadership, not a durable named catalyst, and a single AI wobble can gap the whole index. Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) carries a war-premium bid and oil actually rebounded toward $90 today on renewed Houthi/Gulf risk — but this is a two-sided supply-shock trade, not a clean Sniper. One de-escalation or export-normalization headline and crude gives back premium. Watch-only. The only name that cleared validation is PENG.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, housing, small caps) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.31% and oil feeding inflation fear. But selling bear calls into a VIX this low, with a record-chasing tape that can squeeze shorts on any fresh tech or de-escalation headline, carries its own violent-reversal risk — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~52 is in WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 37% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an active military conflict with oil back near $90 is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, stacked on a bond market at ~5.31% 24-year-high yields and FOMC minutes at 2:00 ET. The scanner boarded only PENG — a genuine Type A double-beat, but on light 0.28x reaction volume and into a headline tape. A record S&P and a low VIX are not a green light when the gap tail is headline-driven and skewed. Stand down on new credit spreads, or push DTE past the headline window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

A $39B 10-year auction and the FOMC minutes (2:00 ET) both land today; a weak auction or hawkish tone could push yields back up and hit rate-sensitive growth, REITs, utilities and small caps hardest.

Oil near $90 / Brent near $101 — crude rebounded from five-week lows on renewed Houthi/Gulf risk; the move is two-sided, but any fresh Hormuz disruption sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical and feeds inflation fear.
FOMC minutes · today 2:00 ET — with the market pricing ~80% odds of a Fed hold, a hawkish tone in the minutes could revive yield pressure; a dovish read supports the Fed-hold trade.
